title: Post hoc analysis of SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6 trials suggests that people with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk treated with semaglutide experience more stable kidney function compared with placebo
authors: Tuttle KR; Bosch-Traberg H; Cherney DZI; et al.
population: T2D at high CV risk; N=6480 (3239 semaglutide/3241 placebo)
primary_endpoint: Annual eGFR slope and persistent >=30%, >=40%, >=50%, or >=57% eGFR decline
key_result: Annual-slope difference +0.59 (0.29-0.89) mL/min/1.73m2; all four persistent-decline HR point estimates below 1 overall and numerically lower at baseline eGFR 30-<60, without detected treatment-by-eGFR interaction
limitations: PubMed abstract does not report the four threshold-specific HRs/CIs/P values; version of record not acquired; multiple post hoc thresholds and non-kidney-enriched CVOT populations

title: Effects of Semaglutide on Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
authors: Perkovic V; Tuttle KR; Rossing P; et al.
population: T2D + CKD; eGFR 25-75 with two enrollment pathways by UACR; on max tolerated/labeled RASi; N=3533 (1767/1766)
primary_endpoint: 5-component composite: sustained >=50% eGFR decline, persistent eGFR<15, chronic KRT initiation, kidney death, CV death
key_result: Primary composite 331 (18.7%) vs 410 (23.2%), HR 0.76 (0.66-0.88) P=0.0003, NNT 20 (14-40) @3y; kidney-specific 4-component composite 218 (12.3%) vs 260 (14.7%) HR 0.79 (0.66-0.94); CV death alone HR 0.71 (0.56-0.89); total eGFR slope diff 1.16 (0.86-1.47) mL/min/1.73m2/yr; baseline-to-week-12 eGFR change -1.07 vs -1.05, difference -0.03 (-0.56 to 0.51), showing no semaglutide-specific differential dip through week 12 while not excluding an earlier resolved transient; chronic week-12-to-end slope -2.36 vs -3.30, difference +0.94 (0.62-1.26); MACE HR 0.82 (0.68-0.98); all-cause death HR 0.80 (0.67-0.95); week-156 MACE/mortality NNTs are sourced separately to FLOW-CKDSEVERITY-2025
limitations: Crossed the efficacy boundary at the prespecified approximately 570-event interim; 741/854 planned events had accrued by final database lock after the stop recommendation; confirmatory secondaries not GSD-adjusted; only 15.6% baseline SGLT2i, 7.3% MRA (0 finerenone); not powered for kidney-failure components alone; mostly White population; industry-sponsored (Novo Nordisk)

title: Effects of semaglutide with and without concomitant SGLT2 inhibitor use in participants with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease in the FLOW trial
authors: Mann JFE; Rossing P; Bakris G; et al.
population: FLOW participants by baseline SGLT2i use: users n=550 (277/273) vs non-users n=2983 (1490/1493)
primary_endpoint: Primary 5-component composite (sustained >=50% eGFR decline, persistent eGFR<15, chronic KRT, kidney death, or CV death) and kidney-specific 4-component composite, by baseline SGLT2i subgroup
key_result: Primary composite: users HR 1.07 (0.69-1.67) vs non-users HR 0.73 (0.63-0.85), P-interaction=0.109; kidney-specific composite: users HR 1.18 (0.71-1.98) vs non-users HR 0.75 (0.61-0.90), P-interaction=0.100; sustained >=50% eGFR-decline component: users HR 1.30 (0.76-2.26), 30/277 vs 23/273, non-users HR 0.66 (0.53-0.83), 135/1489 vs 190/1493, nominal P-interaction=0.023; creatinine total-slope differences +0.75 (-0.01 to 1.50) vs +1.25 (0.91-1.58), P-interaction=0.237; post hoc cystatin-C five-component HR 0.74 (0.47-1.16) vs 0.70 (0.60-0.82), P-interaction=0.844; cystatin-C slope differences +0.92 (0.16-1.68) vs +1.55 (1.21-1.88), P-interaction=0.142; week-104 cystatin-C change differences +3.5 (1.6-5.4) vs +3.4 (2.5-4.2), P-interaction=0.901; exposure-defined semaglutide effects HR 0.88 vs 0.70, P-interaction=0.169; time-varying-SGLT2i-adjusted semaglutide-vs-placebo coefficient HR 0.75 (0.65-0.86), not an ever-vs-never effect; UACR reduction 24% vs 34%, P-interaction=0.279
limitations: Subgroup underpowered (only 79 primary events in SGLT2i-user stratum); baseline and subsequent SGLT2i exposure were non-randomized; asymmetric post-randomization initiation has no identifiable bias direction; hard-composite HRs 1.07/1.18 and wide CIs remain compatible with incremental benefit, null effect, or harm; isolated component P-interaction=0.023 is unadjusted for multiplicity and does not prove harm or true effect modification; post hoc cystatin-C concordance does not establish additivity
evidence_level: High (subgroup analysis; insufficient for definitive additive-benefit claim)

title: Effects of Semaglutide With or Without Concomitant Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist Use in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease: A FLOW Trial Prespecified Secondary Analysis
authors: Rossing P; Bakris G; Perkovic V; et al.
population: FLOW participants by baseline MRA use: users n=257 (136/121; spironolactone 218, eplerenone 38, esaxerenone 1, finerenone 0) vs non-users n=3276 (1631/1645)
primary_endpoint: Primary 5-component composite (sustained >=50% eGFR decline, persistent eGFR<15, chronic KRT, kidney death, or CV death), by baseline MRA subgroup
key_result: MRA users: 23/136 (16.9%) vs 36/121 (29.8%), HR 0.51 (0.30-0.86), 59 events; non-users: 308/1631 (18.9%) vs 374/1645 (22.7%), HR 0.79 (0.68-0.92), 682 events; P-interaction=0.12; exploratory 3-year NNT: users 9, non-users 23; kidney-specific 4-component P-interaction=0.068; RRT-component P-interaction=0.027 (only 11 events, uncorrected)
limitations: Baseline MRA users were predominantly spironolactone/eplerenone; zero baseline finerenone users (not yet approved during FLOW recruitment, 2019-2021); explicitly exploratory subgroup per authors; subgroup NNTs not to be treated as trial-level; cannot support a semaglutide+finerenone additive-efficacy claim
evidence_level: High for overall FLOW effect; exploratory subgroup with no detected heterogeneity; semaglutide+finerenone specifically not established

title: Cardiovascular outcomes with semaglutide by severity of chronic kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: the FLOW trial
authors: Mahaffey KW; Tuttle KR; Arici M; et al.
population: FLOW participants by eGFR (<60/>=60), UACR (<300/>=300), and KDIGO risk class (low-moderate/high/very-high)
primary_endpoint: CV death/MI/stroke and all-cause death, by CKD-severity strata
key_result: Overall CV death/MI/stroke HR 0.82 (0.68-0.98); by eGFR: <60 HR 0.87 (0.71-1.06), >=60 HR 0.59 (0.37-0.94) P-interaction .13; by UACR: <300 HR 1.04 (0.72-1.51), >=300 HR 0.75 (0.61-0.93) P-interaction .13; by KDIGO: low/moderate 0.67 (0.27-1.67), high 0.75 (0.50-1.12), very-high 0.84 (0.68-1.04) P-interaction .79; all-cause death overall HR 0.80 (0.67-0.95); all-cause death by UACR: <300 HR 1.17 (0.83-1.65) vs >=300 HR 0.70 (0.57-0.85) P-interaction=.01; nonfatal MI by eGFR: <60 HR 0.94 (0.63-1.39) vs >=60 HR 0.28 (0.09-0.87) P-interaction=.04; NNT (wk156): CV death/MI/stroke 45 (23-623), all-cause death 39 (21-238)
limitations: Historical local transcription misassigned the Figure 2 eGFR>=60 and KDIGO low/moderate/very-high values; the local reference file was corrected and the full matrix visually rechecked against the published Figure 2 image (PMCID PMC11931213) on 2026-09-05. Earlier/cached copies remain unsafe. The two significant interactions (UACR-mortality P=.01; eGFR-MI P=.04) are 2 of 15 uncorrected interaction tests and are judged likely due to chance by the trial's own authors

title: Effects of Semaglutide on Heart Failure Outcomes in Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease in the FLOW Trial
authors: Pratley RE; Tuttle KR; Rossing P; et al.
population: FLOW participants by baseline HF status: HF present n=678 (342/336) vs absent
primary_endpoint: HF event or CV death (composite); HF events alone; CV death alone; by baseline HF status
key_result: Composite HR 0.73 (0.62-0.87) P=0.0005; HF events alone HR 0.73 (0.58-0.92) P=0.0068; CV death alone HR 0.71 (0.56-0.89) P=0.0036; similar with (HR ~0.73) and without (HR ~0.72) baseline HF
limitations: Abstract-level only (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 version of record; automated full-text retrieval returned HTTP 403, a route failure not a closed-access finding); NYHA/HFrEF-HFpEF breakdown not verified; does not establish FLOW as a dedicated HF-outcomes trial

title: Kidney and Survival Outcomes with Semaglutide by CKD Severity in the FLOW Trial
authors: Tuttle KR; Mann JFE; Mayrdorfer MM; et al.
prespecified_or_posthoc: Prespecified for primary-outcome/eGFR/UACR analyses; post hoc for all-cause-death analyses by CKD severity
population: FLOW participants by baseline eGFR (<30 to >=60) and UACR (<100 to >=2000 mg/g) severity strata
primary_endpoint: Primary 5-component composite (sustained >=50% eGFR decline, persistent eGFR<15, chronic KRT, kidney death, or CV death) and all-cause death, by eGFR/UACR severity strata
key_result: Restates FLOW's own overall counts (primary composite 331/1767 vs 410/1766, HR 0.76 [0.66-0.88]; all-cause death 227/1767 vs 279/1766, HR 0.80 [0.67-0.95]) stratified by severity, not a separate cohort; prespecified primary-outcome analysis consistent across eGFR (P-interaction .83; Fig.1), including eGFR<30 subgroup n=400, 73/218 vs 67/182, HR 0.81 (0.58-1.13), and UACR (P-interaction .42; Fig.2); baseline-reclassified UACR<100 subgroup n=350, 13/177 vs 17/173, HR 0.70 (0.34-1.44), Fig.2; post hoc death estimate lowest at UACR>=2000 mg/g, HR 0.47 (0.31-0.70), P-interaction=.02 (Fig.5)
limitations: Official CC BY 4.0 PMC full text (PMCID PMC13143484) read directly on 2026-09-05; protocol screening required UACR >100/>300, so the imprecise baseline UACR<100 reclassification subgroup is not a prospectively eligible persistent-low-UACR cohort; no subgroup multiplicity adjustment or alpha protection and no subgroup power estimates; mortality-by-severity analyses were post hoc; UACR>=2000 mortality signal is exploratory and not proof of effect modification or larger absolute benefit; distinct from FLOW-CVPHENOTYPE-2026 - do not merge
evidence_level: High for prespecified primary-outcome analyses; Exploratory for post hoc mortality-by-severity analyses

title: Kidney and Survival Benefits of Semaglutide in Diabetes With Chronic Kidney Disease: FLOW Trial Cardiovascular Subgroup Analyses
authors: Tuttle KR; Bakris GL; Baeres FMM; et al.
population: FLOW by baseline ASCVD (n=1198), heart failure (n=678), or high total-CVD-risk without established CVD (PREVENT>=20%, n=1329 of 2000 without ASCVD/HF)
primary_endpoint: Primary 5-component composite (sustained >=50% eGFR decline, persistent eGFR<15, chronic KRT, kidney death, or CV death) and all-cause death, by CV phenotype
key_result: Primary-outcome HR: ASCVD 0.80 (0.63-1.02) vs no ASCVD 0.74 (0.62-0.89), P-interaction=.62; HF 0.67 (0.49-0.93) vs no HF 0.79 (0.67-0.93), P-interaction=.40; high-risk-no-CVD 0.73 (0.58-0.91) vs non-high-risk 0.73 (0.49-1.08), P-interaction=.99. All-cause-death HR: ASCVD 0.82 (0.63-1.07) vs no ASCVD 0.78 (0.62-0.99), P-interaction=.79; HF 0.75 (0.54-1.05) vs no HF 0.81 (0.66-0.99), P-interaction=.74; high-risk 0.71 (0.52-0.95) vs non-high-risk 0.82 (0.47-1.43), P-interaction=.63. Published descriptive 3-year NNTs for these CV phenotypes only: ASCVD 22, HF 13, high-risk-no-CVD 17
limitations: Abstract-level only (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 version of record; automated retrieval returned HTTP 403); no interaction P was below .40, which is failure to detect heterogeneity rather than equivalence; the published NNTs apply only to the three CV-phenotype strata and cannot be extended to KDIGO or UACR strata lacking published stratum-specific ARR/NNT; distinct from FLOW-CKDSEVERITY-2026-CJASN - do not merge

title: Safety of Semaglutide After Dialysis Initiation: An Individual-Level Pooled Analysis
authors: Klein KR; et al.
population: 307 of a source-reported pooled analysis denominator of 34,064 initiated dialysis during follow-up; 165 remained on assigned drug (71 semaglutide/94 placebo)
primary_endpoint: Systematically collected SAEs, MACE, and discontinuation after dialysis initiation
key_result: Among the selected on-treatment cohort, SAEs were 32/71 (45%) vs 54/94 (57%), permanent discontinuation 8.5% vs 10.6%, MACE rates 9.7 vs 16.1 and mortality rates 13.8 vs 18.1 per 100 person-years; these are descriptive postrandomization comparisons, not causal efficacy estimates
limitations: ADA copyright/TDM-ML restriction on cached parse - figures were independently verified in the public structured abstract/official article page, never from the private parse alone; four parent trials' nominal randomized Ns sum to 34,084, leaving an unexplained 20-person difference from the source-reported 34,064 analysis denominator; very small selected cohort, post hoc, survivor/selection bias; "no renal dose adjustment" (PK fact) must not be conflated with proven efficacy in dialysis

title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
authors: Marso SP; Bain SC; Consoli A; et al.
prespecified_or_posthoc: Primary (CV); renal and retinopathy composites secondary
population: T2D at high CV risk, N=3297 (1648/1649)
primary_endpoint: 3-point MACE (primary); nephropathy composite and retinopathy-complication composite (secondary)
key_result: MACE HR 0.74 (0.58-0.95): prespecified noninferiority achieved, with only post hoc/non-prespecified nominal evidence for superiority; nephropathy composite HR 0.64 (0.46-0.88) P=0.005, 62/1648 (3.8%) vs 100/1649 (6.1%); new persistent macroalbuminuria component alone 2.5% vs 4.9%; retinopathy complications HR 1.76 (1.11-2.78) P=0.02, 50 (3.0%) vs 29 (1.8%)
limitations: Trial was powered/prespecified for CV noninferiority, not superiority; nephropathy composite dominated by reduced new-onset persistent macroalbuminuria, not hard kidney endpoints; exact hard-component (creatinine-doubling/RRT/renal-death) event counts not recoverable from any source reached (NEJM full text paywalled to every attempt); retinopathy-complication outcome was prespecified, externally adjudicated, secondary and not multiplicity protected; serial retinal imaging/progression grading was not built into the trial
evidence_level: High (prespecified MACE noninferiority; abstract/secondary-verified); pre-FLOW hypothesis-generating for hard kidney endpoints

title: Semaglutide, reduction in glycated haemoglobin and the risk of diabetic retinopathy
authors: Vilsboll T; Bain SC; Leiter LA; et al.
prespecified_or_posthoc: Prespecified retinopathy-complication endpoint; post hoc explanatory analyses
population: SUSTAIN-6 T2D high-CV-risk population
primary_endpoint: Time to first diabetic-retinopathy complication, externally adjudicated
limitations: Secondary endpoint without multiplicity protection; trial lacked standardized retinal photographs/imaging and formal retinopathy grading; post hoc analyses suggest an early-worsening association with rapid HbA1c decline in participants with pre-existing retinopathy and insulin use, not proof of direct retinal toxicity
evidence_level: Supportive safety signal; mechanism explanatory only

title: Oral Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
authors: Husain M; Birkenfeld AL; Donsmark M; et al.
population: T2D at high CV/renal risk, N=3183 (1591/1592)
primary_endpoint: 3-point MACE (noninferiority)
key_result: MACE 61/1591 (3.8%) vs 76/1592 (4.8%), HR 0.79 (0.57-1.11); noninferiority met (P<0.001) but CI crosses 1, superiority not demonstrated; median follow-up 15.9 months
limitations: No dedicated renal composite; UACR never collected at all; short follow-up limits any renal signal; underpowered/too short for standalone renal conclusions
evidence_level: High (MACE; primary structured abstract verified); no kidney evidence

title: Effect of semaglutide on kidney function across different levels of baseline HbA1c, blood pressure, body weight and albuminuria in SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6
authors: Apperloo EM; Cherney DZI; Kuhlman AB; et al.
population: T2D at high CV risk (pooled 2 RCTs), N=6480 with eGFR data
primary_endpoint: eGFR slope by baseline subgroup
key_result: Pooled eGFR-slope difference 0.59 (0.29-0.89) mL/min/1.73m2/yr; SUSTAIN-6 alone 0.60 (0.24-0.96); consistent across HbA1c/BP/BMI strata (all P-interaction>0.5) and UACR strata (SUSTAIN-6-only subset, P-interaction 0.99)
limitations: Published online 2024, print issue 2025 - label as post hoc, pre-FLOW evidence; smaller magnitude than FLOW; not a dedicated-CKD population (PIONEER-6 excluded eGFR<30)

title: Potential kidney protection with liraglutide and semaglutide: exploratory mediation analysis
authors: Mann JFE; Buse JB; Idorn T; et al.
population: LEADER N=9340 (605 kidney events); SUSTAIN-6 N=3297 (162 kidney events)
primary_endpoint: Mediated fraction of kidney-composite effect via HbA1c, systolic BP, body weight (CV-death-excluded composite, different from FLOW's own)
key_result: HbA1c mediated 25% (LEADER, 95% CI -7.1 to 67.3) / 26% (SUSTAIN-6, CI noncalculable); systolic BP mediated 9% (LEADER, 2.8-22.7) / 22% (SUSTAIN-6, CI noncalculable); body weight mediated 9% (LEADER, -7.9 to 35.5) / 0% (SUSTAIN-6, CI noncalculable and therefore uninformative rather than evidence of absent mediation)
limitations: Each candidate mediator and each trial were analyzed separately (only the SUSTAIN-6 dose arms were pooled); effects cannot be added and no joint mediation estimate exists. Different (CV-death-excluded, macroalbuminuria/creatinine-doubling-based) kidney composite than FLOW's own primary outcome; most CIs wide or noncalculable; not FLOW-specific, not re-tested within FLOW's own population

title: Change in KDIGO Risk Category With Semaglutide in SUSTAIN-6
authors: Tuttle KR; et al.
population: SUSTAIN-6 population
primary_endpoint: KDIGO risk-category movement
key_result: Change in UACR was the main driver of favorable KDIGO risk-category movement; eGFR change drove progression mainly in already-high-risk stratum
limitations: Post hoc, low-power (most participants had preserved baseline kidney function); consistent with an albuminuria-dominant pre-FLOW signal

title: Long-term kidney outcomes of semaglutide in obesity and cardiovascular disease in the SELECT trial
authors: Colhoun HM; Lingvay I; Brown PM; et al.
population: Overweight/obesity + established CVD, WITHOUT diagnosed diabetes (HbA1c<6.5% at entry; 66.4% prediabetic, 33.5% normoglycemic), N=17,604 (8803/8801)
primary_endpoint: Composite: kidney-disease death, chronic KRT initiation, persistent eGFR<15, persistent >=50% eGFR decline, or onset of persistent macroalbuminuria; continuous eGFR and UACR outcomes
key_result: Composite HR 0.78 (0.63-0.96), P=.02; 1.8% vs 2.2%. Week-104 eGFR difference +0.75 (0.43-1.06), and +2.19 (1.00-3.38) in baseline eGFR<60; total slope +0.39 (0.30-0.48), chronic week-20-to-end slope +0.29 (0.18-0.40), and European-subset acute baseline-to-week-16 slope -1.33 (-2.68 to 0.02) mL/min/1.73m2/yr; week-104 UACR relative difference -10.7% (-13.2 to -8.2), with baseline-UACR strata <30: -8.1% (-10.6 to -5.6), 30-<300: -27.2% (-35.3 to -18.1), >=300: -31.4% (-54.9 to 4.3). Event effect driven by macroalbuminuria onset and >=50% eGFR-decline components; weight mediation of week-104 eGFR change estimated at 81% (41-120%)
limitations: No diabetes-specific dedicated CKD population; different dose (2.4mg) from FLOW; composite includes softer macroalbuminuria-onset component and hard components were sparse; continuous outcomes were secondary and P values unadjusted; eGFR<60 rise in both arms may partly reflect regression to mean; acute slope evaluable only in a European subset; only ~1/5 had eGFR<60 or UACR>=30; mediation was on eGFR change, not the hard composite, and was suggestive rather than definitive
evidence_level: High for prespecified SELECT secondary outcomes; extrapolation to dedicated albuminuric CKD requires caution

title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes
authors: Lincoff AM; Brown-Frandsen K; Colhoun HM; et al.
population: Overweight/obesity + established CVD, no diabetes, N=17,604
primary_endpoint: 3-point MACE
key_result: Cited only for population/dose/design context supporting SELECT-KIDNEY-2024 and for parent-trial sample-size reconciliation in the dialysis safety discussion

title: Effect of Semaglutide on Regression and Progression of Glycemia in People With Overweight or Obesity but Without Diabetes in the SELECT Trial
authors: Kahn SE; Deanfield JE; Jeppesen OK; et al.

limitations: Primary PMC article (PMCID PMC11282386) identifies a prespecified secondary analysis; baseline glycemic characterization is used only to show that 'without diabetes' is not equivalent to 'without dysglycemia' and does not establish kidney-effect mediation

title: Oral Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes
authors: McGuire DK; Marx N; Mulvagh SL; et al.
population: T2D + ASCVD and/or CKD, N=9650 (4825/4825)
primary_endpoint: 3-point MACE
key_result: 579/4825 (12.0%) vs 668/4825 (13.8%), HR 0.86 (0.77-0.96) P=0.006; confirmatory secondary outcomes (incl. kidney composite) did not differ significantly per abstract; mean follow-up 47.5+/-10.9 months
limitations: Population had more preserved kidney function than FLOW (mean eGFR ~74); UACR not collected; also cited for parent-trial sample-size reconciliation in the dialysis safety discussion

title: Impact of Oral Semaglutide on Kidney Outcomes in People With Type 2 Diabetes: Results From the SOUL Randomized Trial
authors: Mann JFE; Marx N; Deanfield JE; et al.
population: T2D + ASCVD and/or CKD, N=9650, mean eGFR 73.8, UACR not collected
primary_endpoint: Five-point kidney/CV-death composite (persistent >=50% eGFR decline, persistent eGFR<15, chronic KRT, kidney death, or CV death); four-point composite excl. CV death; eGFR slope
key_result: 5-point composite: 403/4825 (8.4%) vs 435/4825 (9.0%), HR 0.91 (0.80-1.05) P=0.19 - NOT significant; 4-point (excl. CV death): 112/4825 vs 129/4825, HR 0.86 (0.66-1.10) P=0.22; eGFR-slope difference 0.40 (0.27-0.53) mL/min/1.73m2/yr, nominal P<0.0001 favoring semaglutide; placebo-arm kidney-composite event rate ~2.3/100 patient-yr (~1/3 of FLOW's 7.5/100 patient-yr)
limitations: Kidney composite was nonsignificant; lower baseline kidney risk and fewer events are an author-offered explanation, not a proven causal attribution, and dose/route cannot be isolated; ADA copyright/TDM-ML restriction on cached parse - cite via independently verified abstract text only, never as sole basis; once the kidney composite failed, the eGFR slope and all further SOUL secondary analyses are formally exploratory under the prespecified testing hierarchy
evidence_level: Suggestive/formally exploratory (nominal eGFR slope after gate failure); Not significant (composite kidney outcome)

title: Effect of semaglutide on kidney outcomes in the SELECT, FLOW, and SOUL trials: a prespecified pooled analysis
authors: Mann JFE; Badve SV; Baeres FMM; et al.
population: N=30,787 pooled across 3 trials (FLOW=T2D+CKD 1.0mg SC; SELECT=established ASCVD w/o diabetes 2.4mg SC; SOUL=T2D+ASCVD/CKD 14mg oral); mean follow-up 39.5-47.5 months
primary_endpoint: Primary pooled composite: persistent >=50% eGFR decline, kidney failure (persistent eGFR<15 or KRT), kidney death, or CV death; narrower secondary excludes CV death

title: A FIDELITY Analysis on Finerenone With SGLT2i and GLP-1RA in CKD
authors: Singh AK; et al.
population: FIDELITY N=12990; 167 used SGLT2i+GLP-1RA at baseline
primary_endpoint: UACR, eGFR and BP trajectories; safety
key_result: Finerenone improved surrogate trajectories across concomitant-treatment strata; most frequent GLP-1RA/SGLT2i pair was liraglutide/empagliflozin
limitations: Only 167 triple-therapy baseline users; background drugs not randomized; surrogate analyses; not semaglutide-specific hard-outcome evidence

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Finerenone Added to SGLT2 Inhibitor and GLP-1RA Therapy in T2D and CKD
authors: Nakhleh A; et al.
population: T2D+CKD on SGLT2i plus liraglutide/dulaglutide/semaglutide; N=51
primary_endpoint: UACR, eGFR and potassium at about 26 weeks
key_result: At median 27 weeks adjusted UACR change -51.3%; eGFR change -3.92 mL/min/1.73m2; potassium +0.34 mmol/L
limitations: No counterfactual; only 51 participants; GLP-1RA molecules pooled; surrogate/short-term; confounding and regression to mean; no hard-outcome inference

title: Rapid and Simultaneous Initiation of Four Guideline-Directed CKD Therapies (RAPID-CKD)
authors: study investigators
population: T2D+CKD; planned N=64
primary_endpoint: Six-month retention, UACR, eGFR and safety/feasibility outcomes
key_result: Registry status NOT_YET_RECRUITING at 2026-09-05; estimated start 2026-04-30; no results
limitations: Small feasibility/surrogate pilot, not powered for hard kidney outcomes; stale estimated start versus recruitment status must be preserved rather than reconciled by assumption
